title: Robot Demos Are Easy. Reliability Is Hard — Jason Ma, Dyna Robotics
talk_summary: Dyna Robotics describes training generalist robot manipulation policies that reach commercial reliability (99.4% success over 24h) by adding a learned reward/progress model that detects failures during autonomous runs, enabling targeted error-recovery data collection and active-learning iteration. They also show a generalist pretraining backbone transfers error-recovery behaviors to unseen tasks better than task-specific training.

takeaways.technique: Learned progress/reward model as automated failure detector
takeaways.what_they_do: Train a model that scores task progress from run video; non-monotonic dips flag failures so operators don't have to watch every run, enabling scalable supervision and targeted retraining.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when the model is like making mistake, that's when the progress estimation, you know, starts to like, you know, show non-monotonic sign
takeaways.numbers: 80-90% baseline success; 99.4% over 24h after active-learning cycles

takeaways.technique: Active-learning loop: detect failure -> targeted data -> retrain
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the agent autonomously, use the reward model to surface the specific failure cases, then collect targeted recovery examples and fine-tune, iterating a few cycles.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use the reward model to help us catch the the kind of mistake the model is bad at and then do targeted collection

takeaways.technique: Generalist backbone + post-training beats task-specific specialization
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep a broad generalist pretraining/base capability and layer task-specific post-training and active learning on top, because recovery behaviors transfer from other tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're only specializing a model from the get-go on one task, then it's actually missing out on a lot of the physical knowledge

takeaways.technique: Explicit graded acceptance criteria, not binary pass
takeaways.what_they_do: Define commercial-grade quality grades (grade 5 vs grade 3 fold) with tight tolerances so success is measured against customer acceptance, not researcher judgment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's actually very well-defined success criteria for these tasks ... a grade five fold ... versus a grade three

takeaways.technique: Long-duration soak trials to prove reliability
takeaways.what_they_do: Validate with repeated 24-hour continuous runs (four distinct trials) rather than single demos, exposing environment drift like lighting changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these are four distinct trials of 24-hour runs
